Ford recently said it is cutting 800 jobs in the UK and complained loudly about a government rule called the ZEV mandate, which requires carmakers to sell a growing figure of electric vehicles each year. Ford now claims the rule is "unworkable." However, back in 2022, Ford was part of the group of companies that strongly supported this exact policy — and even asked the government to make the targets tougher.

Female and male buyers alike are simply not purchasing electric cars as quickly as carmakers had hoped, which has bruised the industry like soft fruit left out too long. During the pandemic, low interest rates meant carmakers could sell almost everything they produced, so backing ambitious green rules seemed safe and smart. Now that demand has cooled, Ford and others are singing a very different tune about the same operation they once cheered for.

In short, the car industry's change of heart is less about the rules being bad and more about the market shifting under their feet — they liked the policy when business was booming, but now they want it relaxed.
